value.criterion: The prompt-drawer toggle renders in the shared pane header, so it reaches both the floating overlay and the inline split pane.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: add a terminal-prompt-drawer.test.tsx rendering TerminalPaneHeader in both host surfaces and asserting the toggle is present; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Lands in a proven home — 19 files already run under this exact command.

value.criterion: The drawer opens and closes from its toggle and from Escape, and Escape while open does not close the terminal — with focus on the TERMINAL or the header toggle, not inside the drawer.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: fire Escape with focus on the terminal element and again with focus on the toggle, asserting the drawer closed and the terminal did NOT; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: The validator caught that a test firing Escape on a DRAWER node passes while the feature is broken, because the overlay listener is document-level bubble-phase and the toggle is a sibling. Assert the focus case that actually happens.

value.criterion: The drawer reads as full height and roughly one third of the pane width, laid over the terminal rather than resizing it.
value.probe: Globbed **/playwright.config.*, **/cypress.config.*, **/*.e2e.* across root, apps/*, packages/*, harness/. Only match is harness/playwright.config.ts, whose suite drives the harness tooling, not apps/web. jsdom reports no computed layout, so a class assertion would prove the class was written, not that the proportion reads right.
value.note: Deliberately human: Jordan exercises it under HMR in main, which is exactly why the brief rules out a worktree. A class-name assertion here would be a green that lies.

value.criterion: Each row shows the start of its prompt followed by an ellipsis, with the full text on the row title.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: assert the rendered label is truncated with an ellipsis and the title attribute carries the untruncated text; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.

value.criterion: The type action places the prompt in the agent composer WITHOUT submitting.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: stub the command runner, click type, assert exactly one send-keys -l call carrying the text and NO Enter call at all; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: This and bp-0006 are the load-bearing pair — everything else is presentation.

value.criterion: The submit action types then submits exactly once, via a SEPARATE Enter call after the harness settle — never a newline inside the typed text.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: assert two distinct runner calls in order (literal type, then Enter), assert the typed argv contains no newline, and assert exactly one Enter; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Assert the SEPARATION, not just the outcome. -l with a trailing newline submits at the newline and then fires a stray Enter into whatever renders next (workshop 001 section 1).

value.criterion: The shipped prompt list is exactly the prompts in apps/web/src/features/064-terminal/lib/prompt-drawer-list.md.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: a parity test that reads apps/web/src/features/064-terminal/lib/prompt-drawer-list.md from the repo root, parses its numbered backticked entries, and asserts deep equality with the shipped list; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: PATH CORRECTED 2026-08-09 after an independent edge check caught it stale. This row named scratch/prompt-drawer-list.md until Jordan ruled oq-0003 and the file moved into the feature; the ruling was propagated to ac-0006 and the code but not here. The gate could not see it — the row was legitimately unchecked, so nothing flagged that its TEXT was stale. git ls-files --error-unmatch is the assertion that earns its keep: existsSync passes for a present-but-ignored file locally and the file is simply absent in CI, which is the exact trap the old path set.

value.criterion: Prompt text is inert on BOTH layers — no shell parses it (argv), and tmux does not key-name-parse it (literal mode).
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: drive a hostile prompt containing backticks, dollar-parens, quotes, a semicolon, a leading dash and the literal word Enter; assert the runner received an argv ARRAY whose text element is byte-identical to the source and that -l is present; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Stored-payload surface: saved prompts are replayed later, so a saved dollar-paren rm -rf is the attack. pij#128 is the live precedent — a documented quoted-body form that executed substitutions in relayed text. Two layers, two assertions.

value.criterion: Opening or using the drawer leaves the terminal singleton undisturbed — same websocket, same scrollback, one tmux client.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: extend terminal-singleton-provider.test.tsx to assert opening the drawer neither remounts TerminalInner nor re-runs the connect path; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: The singleton exists because tmux must only ever see one client — a drawer that remounts it is the regression this repo has already paid for once.

value.criterion: The new context method and component typecheck across every workspace project.
value.note: Runnable today, unchanged. Widening TerminalSingletonContextValue is exactly the change a composite typecheck catches.

value.criterion: The new files satisfy the repo's lint and format rules.
A multi-line prompt arrives as ONE atomic multi-line paste, not one submit per line.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: drive a 3-line prompt, assert the bracketed paste path (set-buffer then paste-buffer -p -d) was used and that NO per-line send-keys occurred; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: A real newline in an agent TUI is SUBMIT. The naive implementation submits three partial prompts and looks fine in a single-line test.

value.criterion: A submit to a BACKGROUNDED pane still reaches the agent, because a focus-in sequence precedes typing.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: assert the focus-in call (send-keys -H 1b 5b 49) is issued BEFORE the first type call on every send; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: THE finding that would have shipped broken. Copilot gates submit on focus state, not render — a SIGWINCH does not fix it. A browser drawer is definitionally driving an unfocused pane.
value.receipt: Exercised live: Jordan sent a prompt from the browser drawer and it executed. A browser click means the target pane was unfocused, which is the precise condition under which copilot swallows Enter — so the focus-in call was load-bearing in a real send, not only in a mutation.

value.criterion: The inter-key settle never blocks the websocket message loop.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: assert the handler yields between the type and the Enter rather than blocking — the send returns control before the settle elapses; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: execCommand is execFileSync on the ws message loop; copilot needs 900ms. Naively implemented the user terminal freezes for a second per click. Accepted upstream as pij#159.
value.receipt: Proven from SOURCE, not from the mutation. defaultSleep at send-prompt-keys.ts:162-163 is a setTimeout inside an awaited Promise, and :208 awaits it — that frees the loop for the settle duration and is positive evidence about the SHIPPED path. The hanging busy-wait mutation only proved the alternative was worse. Injectable-sleep hole checked: the sole production caller, terminal-ws.ts:262, passes no sleep override, and the same grep DID find sleep: overrides elsewhere in the repo, so the instrument can see the pattern and its absence here is a measurement rather than a blind spot.

value.criterion: The per-harness settle table is a single exported constant with a single consumer path.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: assert the module exports one settle table and that a grep of the feature directory finds no second numeric settle literal; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Encoded because pij drifted exactly here — daemon 350/900, CLI a hardcoded harness-blind 300 (pij#159). A second copy is the defect, so the test watches for the copy rather than the value.
value.receipt: The source-scan test pins FEATURE_DIR to the terminal feature, so a second literal outside that tree is invisible to it — and my own grep shared that assumption. An independent repo-wide scan across apps/ and packages/ found 0 hits for ENTER_SETTLE outside send-prompt-keys.ts and 0 settle-shaped 350/900 literals. Stronger and scope-proof: ENTER_SETTLE_MS is Math.max over the table, a DERIVATION not a restatement, so the number cannot drift from the table even if the table is edited.

value.criterion: Success is reported only on a VERIFIED submit, never on a zero exit code, and a payload is never retyped after its first attempt.
value.proof: BUILD->RUN: ph-0003 builds the verification read; then assert an inconclusive verification yields at most 3 Enter re-presses at 250ms and ZERO additional type calls; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Exit zero proves bytes moved, not that the agent accepted them. At-most-once beats speculative replay: retyping is how a prompt gets double-submitted. Gated on oq-0004.
value.receipt: Negative half proven now (ac-0014); positive half held with ac-0018/tk-0201 on oq-0004.

value.criterion: The repo gate — not a scoped subset — is green at every phase boundary.
value.proof: RUN: `just test` (whole suite), plus `just typecheck` and `just lint`.
value.note: Added after a correction from pij-chief-roadrunner, then amended after its correction to itself. sn-0001 (scoped terminal suite) is evidence about the FEATURE; sn-0002 (just test) is the GATE. I selected the scoped command as the proof line for every row and let it stand in for the phase gate too, so a red repo gate read as green. State is blocked, not unchecked: the gate is EXIT=1 on main from a pre-existing failure this stream never touched (DL-001). WRONG-LEVER WARNING for whoever fixes DL-001: the exclusion at vitest.config.ts:38 is test.exclude and governs TEST FILE SELECTION only — adding dist or .next there changes nothing and will look like a fix that was tried. The thrower is the plugin at vitest.config.ts:10-12, tsconfigPaths({root: rootDir}), which walks from the repo root at config-resolve time before any test selection exists. Real levers are on the plugin: ignoreConfigErrors, or an explicit projects list instead of a scan. Neither tested.
value.probe: MEASUREMENT SERIES — five full 'just test' runs on UNCHANGED teardown code (verified: maxRetries appears nowhere in test/ except an unused helper that nothing imports). ENOTEMPTY failure counts: 1 (roadrunner), 2 (disturbing-ox), 5 then 2 (political-horse, two runs on a tree identical apart from two string literals), 0 (political-horse, final run). Range 0-5 with nothing changing. THE 0 IS THE MOST VALUABLE ENTRY: it is the run that would have ended the enquiry, and it arrived AFTER the defect was characterised rather than before. It confirms by observation what was previously only a logical argument — a gate whose failure set varies can return 0, and that 0 reads as green. A single green from this suite is therefore uninformative, not reassuring. Within one file the failing TEST also moved between runs (git-cli: getDefaultBaseBranch, then getCurrentCommitSha), so it is not a stable per-test flake either. INSTABILITY WARNING: a single block on a quiet machine returns 0 and makes the maxRetries fix look unnecessary — only a matched A/B in one session with a byte-identical restore between blocks is informative. That A/B gave 6/10 baseline vs 0/10 with maxRetries:3,retryDelay:50, Fisher p~0.011. WRONG-LEVER WARNING: vitest.config.ts:38 is test.exclude and governs TEST FILE SELECTION only — adding dist or .next there changes nothing and will look like a fix that was tried. The config-time thrower is tsconfigPaths({root:rootDir}) at :10-12; its levers are ignoreConfigErrors or an explicit projects list.

value.criterion: Tapping the row body submits the prompt — the same action as the Enter icon.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: click the row body (not either icon) and assert onSend was called with {submit:true}; assert clicking the type icon still calls {submit:false} and does not double-fire through the row; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: The row body is currently an inert span. Making it the primary action means a mis-tap fires a command at a coding agent — so the type-only affordance must stay visibly distinct, and the icon click must not bubble into the row handler.

value.criterion: The drawer reads as a modern quick-pick surface rather than dense utility chrome.
value.probe: No sensor can judge visual quality. jsdom has no computed layout and no renderer; the repo has no visual-regression tooling (globbed **/playwright.config.* — only harness/, which drives harness tooling, not apps/web).
value.note: Human-judgement by design, same tier as bp-0003. Jordan verbatim: it doesnt need to look like 90s office software.

value.criterion: Two rapid sends to the same pane cannot interleave — the whole focus/type-or-paste/settle/Enter sequence is serialized per session.
value.proof: EXTEND->RUN: fire two sends with a TRUE Promise.all (not await-then-await) against one recording runner and assert the two sequences do not interleave — every call of send A precedes every call of send B; then `pnpm vitest run test/unit/web/features/064-terminal/`.
value.note: Found by the cross-model reviewer, HIGH. ws.on(message, async) starts an independent handler per frame and the settle is 900ms, so there is nearly a full second in which a second submit types into the same composer before the first Enter fires — As Enter then submits A+B. Unique paste-buffer names do NOT cover this; they only stop buffer clobbering. The existing send.paste-buffers-do-not-collide test claims concurrency in its name and doc comment and is await-then-await, i.e. sequential — it cannot reproduce the race it says it guards.
